details: The US Consumer Price Index (CPI) for August remained at 3.4% year-over-year, aligning with market expectations. However, core CPI, excluding volatile food and energy, rose 0.3% month-over-month, slightly above forecasts. Concurrently, the Producer Price Index (PPI) for August increased by 5.4% annually, exceeding the anticipated 5.3%. These inflation figures have heightened market expectations, with an 87% probability now priced in for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike next week. Higher interest rates typically reduce the attractiveness of non-yielding assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: US August Inflation Fuels Fed Rate Hike Bets Amid Mixed Data

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) unanimously decided to raise its key deposit rate by 25 basis points to 2.5%. This marks the second rate increase of the year, with ECB President Christine Lagarde characterizing the decision as a "no-brainer." The move underscores the central bank's firm commitment to combating persistent inflation within the Eurozone, contributing to a broader risk-off sentiment in financial markets. This hawkish stance from a major central bank tends to negatively impact risk assets, including cryptocurrencies.
title: ECB Hikes Deposit Rate to 2.5%, Signaling Continued Fight Against Inflation

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has definitively stated it will not include Bitcoin in its official reserves. The institution cites concerns over Bitcoin's inherent instability, high volatility, lack of liquidity, and potential challenges to monetary sovereignty. Instead, the ECB is concentrating on the development of its own Digital Euro, an electronic version of cash designed to be public, free, and non-speculative, with a planned circulation around 2029. This decision highlights institutional caution towards volatile cryptocurrencies while pursuing state-backed digital currency initiatives.
title: ECB Rules Out Bitcoin for Reserves, Prioritizes Digital Euro

details: Stablecoins are experiencing a significant surge in adoption across various African nations, including Nigeria and Ghana. This growth is primarily driven by the high volatility of local currencies, the expense and inefficiency of traditional banking systems, and complexities in cross-border transactions. Pegged mainly to the US dollar, stablecoins offer African users a more stable and efficient alternative for managing finances, facilitating remittances, and engaging in international trade, thereby bridging traditional and digital financial ecosystems.
title: Stablecoins Gain Traction in Africa Amid Currency Volatility

details: The cryptocurrency market recently experienced a brief rally, notably in Ether, primarily propelled by a significant wave of liquidations of bearish bets, known as short squeezes. This surge occurred as financial markets reacted to a series of US economic reports and declining oil prices. Analysts suggest that these rapid price movements are indicative of speculative trading driving the market rather than sustained, fundamental demand for digital assets.
title: Ether Short Squeezes Fuel Brief Crypto Rally Amid Market Speculation
